name: Focus Ring
summary: The one indicator that says where the keyboard is — why the library draws it on :focus-visible, what the offset is for, the two-tone version that survives any background, and what `outline: none` actually costs.
demoNote: No JavaScript on this page, and it is meant to be Tabbed through rather than read. Example 4 is broken on purpose and live: three buttons, and only one of them can be followed with a keyboard.

contract.useWhen: The visible focus indicator, and what clips or hides one by accident.
keyboard: :focus-visible matches this; :focus also matches a mouse press
failureModes: an overflow:hidden ancestor clipping a positive outline-offset, with nothing to see
border-radius in a focus rule — an outline already follows the element’s own
a sticky bar covering the focused element, which only happens moving backwards (SC 2.4.11)
a ring built out of the border, which a ghost button does not have at rest
